To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the changes of the critical temperature Tc of the YBa_3Cu_3O_7 superconductor with the pressure P are mainly due to the intrinsic contribution, and that the charge transfer contribution is negligible.

the pressure dependence of Tc in the YBa2Cu3O_{7-δ} superconducting family is mainly due to the intrinsic contribution to the critical temperature and that this contribution can be explained in terms of an extended Hubbard model.

(i) the Hubbard model applied to YBa_2CU_3O_{6+\delta} superconductors, under pressure, can be reduced to the BCS model, and (ii) the changes in the critical temperature Tc of YBa_2(Cu_1-xM_x)_3O_{7-x} (M=Zn, Ni) under pressure, are almost due to an intrinsic contribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a microscopic model of the YBa_ 2Cu_3 O_{7- \delta} superconductors.
the effect of pressure on superconducting properties of YBa_2 Cu_3O_{ 7-\delta} in the framework of a BCS-type extended Hubbard model.
a method for studying the pressure effects in high-Tc superconductors based on the Hubbard model.

the pressure effects on Tc are due to a modification of the effective attractive potential V, which is the same in the charge transfer and in the intrinsic mechanism.
the phase diagram Tc(n_h,P) is mainly determined by the intrinsic term.

the pressure dependence of Tc in YBa_2 Cu_3O_{6.95}, YBa_2C u_3O_{ 6.9}, and YBa_2 C u_3O_6.85 is due to the pressure effect on the attractive interaction, and that the charge transfer contribution is negligible in this pressure range.
